lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Raúl, it's Kendra. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walking went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Honestly, rough week. My back is acting up.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to walk 15 minutes on 4 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good! I didn't miss a day.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the walking. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I could walk at the mall, it's air conditioned.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walking fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I think I can do 20 minutes if it's early.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to feel like yourself again.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This feels really necessary to you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, yes. My feet are still numb from the chemo, I'm scared I'll fall.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you try the mall?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You need to walk every day, no excuses.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you use the step counter?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe walk 15 minutes on 5 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the numbness in your feet gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 4 out of 4 days, the hard part was not having a safe place to walk, and next week you're going to walk 15 minutes on 5 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Raúl, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Agenda setting with a closing invitation
Attributes a preference participant did not state
Adds meaning beyond what participant said
Strength asserted, not drawn from participant
Needs to lower blood sugar; wrote on calendar
Need for mental health and doctor support
Numb feet from chemo; fear of falling as barrier
Jumps to mall without exploring fall fear
Reflects openness and need for fit
Reflects movement and desire to continue
Summary; restates barrier as safe place, not fall fear

flags.reason: Participant reports numb feet from chemo and fear of falling; coach moved to mall question without assessing fall risk or safety.
'You need to walk every day, no excuses' is directive and lectures without permission, undercutting autonomy after the participant voiced ambivalence.
Summary reframes the barrier as lacking a safe place and omits the fall fear and numbness the participant raised.

score.summary: Kendra reinforced Raúl's strong adherence and drew out good change talk, including the mall idea, the alarm, and the indoor backup plan. However, she missed the fall-risk concern from his numb feet, used one directive 'no excuses' line, and did not resolve his request to move the next call time.
strengths: Line 9-10: Recognized full adherence and affirmed starting as the hardest part.
Line 28-29: Affirmed Raúl's autonomy and named his ambivalence without pressure.
Line 48-52: Elicited concrete plans (phone alarm, backup indoor walking) that came from him.
coaching_tips: Line 34: When Raúl mentions numb feet and fear of falling, pause and ask about safety before moving to solutions.
Line 40: Replace 'no excuses' with a reflection and an open question, e.g., 'What makes this hard to fit in right now?'
Line 53: Summarize using his own words, including the fear of falling, rather than reframing the barrier.
Line 56: Confirm the new call time before closing so the next contact is actually set.
